brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Keep sewing supplies tidy: separate places for different kinds of supplies
requirements.evidence: 8 compartments in 3 bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-half-div3.

requirements.requirement: Deep spots for tall items and shallow spots for small notions
requirements.evidence: The two full-depth bins are deep and the one half-depth bin is shallow.

requirements.requirement: A sturdy organiser that stays together and has finished edges
requirements.evidence: Solid end caps cover every open side and joint bolts hold the bases together. The check found no rule errors and no parts overlapping.

requirements.requirement: Show it in use with sewing items
requirements.evidence: The catalogue has no sewing props, so a standing marker (prop:1) and pen (prop:2) stand in for marking tools. No prop warnings.

finish.summary:
I built a small sewing organiser from three hex bases set in a triangle, each holding a drop-in bin. That gives 8 compartments:
- A full-depth bin with 3 compartments, for thread spools and tall tools.
- A full-depth bin with 2 compartments, for scissors, a tape measure or fabric scraps.
- A half-depth bin with 3 compartments, for pins, needles, buttons and bobbins.

The open sides are closed with solid end caps, and the joints are bolted so the three cells don't slide apart. The build has 18 parts. The final check found no rule errors and no parts overlapping. The catalogue has no sewing props, so I staged it with a standing marker and pen to show the scale.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
